title: Coverage dimensions
summary: Choose checks for the consequences of a change. Execution percentages describe only part of that evidence.

sections.label: Possible dimensions
rows: Which instructions or branches ran, and what did the assertions check?
Which relevant states, interactions and failure cases were exercised?
Do the affected producer and consumer contracts agree?
Do representative inputs produce the expected meaning and results?
Do applicable schemas or validation rules hold?
Are meaning, scope and applicability preserved?
Do the accepted requirements have meaningful verification?

sections.label: Technology examples
sections.text: Java coverage, React interaction checks and RDF/SPARQL fixtures measure different things. SHACL applies when a project uses shapes to validate RDF. Select relevant dimensions rather than requiring every technology.

sections.label: Aggregation
sections.text: Missing reports mean unknown coverage. Aggregate covered and total units only for comparable metrics. Keep code execution, user scenarios and domain checks distinct. Do not average unrelated percentages.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: The verification plan covers consequences and meaningful scenarios rather than a universal percentage target.

catalog.applicability: Use when planning or judging the verification of a change and an execution percentage is being treated as the whole picture. It lists the other dimensions to consider and the rule for aggregating only comparable metrics.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
